smells.finding: The two new blocks (git diff --name-only ... / assert unstaged == '' ...) and (git ls-files --others --exclude-standard ... / assert untracked == '' ...) share an identical shape: subprocess.run -> .stdout.strip() -> assert == '' with an f-string naming the offender. Non-blocking: a tiny local helper (run_git_empty(args, label)) would remove the duplication, but the two calls are genuinely different git commands answering different halves of the worktree-vs-index question, and keeping them as separate statements gives each its own assert line and its own failure message naming which half tripped (unstaged vs untracked) -- worth more here than deduplicating 4 lines. Leaving as an observation, not a blocker.

The docstring grew substantially, but it explains a genuinely non-obvious git semantic (git status --porcelain conflates worktree-vs-index with index-vs-HEAD) that caused the original defect -- it clarifies WHY the predicate is shaped this way, it does not paper over unclear code. The predicate itself (two named, separately-asserted git reads) is legible without the comment; the comment is load-bearing context for the NEXT person who is tempted to 'simplify' back to git status --porcelain.
